title: Residency enforcement runbook - implementation notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic engineering runbook for implementing residency enforcement and region pinning for Private and Dedicated deployments. Its goal is to document the enforcement model, runtime constraints, step-by-step implementation checklist, telemetry/controls, and rollout plan so teams can execute migrations with predictable risk and observability.

Scope:
- Applies to Private (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated clusters where customer policy requires region residency or legal data residency (EU, UK, CA, AU).
- Covers request routing, storage constraints (KV caches, object stores), model pinning, fallback policies, and audit logging.
- Excludes: hosted multi-tenant service defaults (separate doc).

Context / Why this exists:
We already have design-level decisions in the Regional Residency Spec. Operational gaps surfaced in last two migrations: sticky-session leaks across regions, TTLs for cached KV payloads not region-tagged, and ambiguous fallback behavior when capacity is constrained. This runbook addresses actionable fixes and an ordered rollout to prevent regressions.

Top-level enforcement model (summary):
1) Policy layer: authoritative record for residency is the tenancy profile attached to each customer (customer.metadata.residency = e.g., eu-west-1).
2) Pinning: routing layer must honor pin attribute for all write/read paths (control-plane, request ingress, KV cache).
3) Enforcement points: API ingress, routing proxies, model scheduler, storage gateway.
4) Fallbacks: soft-fallback (same-region compatible model variant) and hard-fallback (deny or queue). Default behavior must be explicit per-customer.

Design decisions (non-obvious):
- We pin at the request-routing layer rather than at the scheduler only. Reason: prevents cross-region latency/egress and enforces KMS/S3 locality constraints earlier in the path.
- Cache objects must be tagged with region and residency_policy hash. Expiry semantics must be conservative during migration windows.
- Fallback priority: 1) identical model in pinned region, 2) quantized/compatible model in pinned region, 3) if allowed by contract then nearby-region with audit, 4) otherwise 403 with human escalation.

Key implementation checklist (ordered, for engineering runbook use):
- [ ] Add residency attribute to tenant profile in control plane (INF-823) and surface in admin API.
- [ ] Expose a per-route residency override flag for product teams (feature flag guarded) so test routes can opt-out.
- [ ] Routing: update edge-proxy to read residency header (X-Residency) and route to region-local gateways. QA: simulate cross-region request with header mismatch.
- [ ] Scheduler/model-serving: ensure model variants are tagged with supported_regions metadata. Reject workload if no compatible variant.
- [ ] Storage gateway: S3/KV writes must include region tag; block writes to out-of-region buckets for pinned tenants. Add pre-write hook + audit event.
- [ ] KV cache: include residency hash in cache key; implement a migration-safe eviction policy.
- [ ] Telemetry: emit residency_enforcement.status, residency_enforcement.reason, residency_enforcement.action for every request. Wire to Console trace view.
- [ ] Audit logs: append tenant.residency, routed_region, model_variant, decision (allowed/blocked/fallback) to every request log stored in long-term audit S3.
- [ ] Policy simulator: implement a read-only mode to run historical traffic against enforcement rules for 7 days to estimate failure modes.
- [ ] Feature flags: enforcement_mode = [off, simulate, enforce]; default simulate during first 2 weeks.
- [ ] Legal/Privacy signoff: create checklist for region-specific data retention and KMS key residency.

Telemetry and SLOs to monitor during rollout:
- Enforcement hit rate (percentage of requests evaluated by residency policy). Target 100% during canary.
- Block rate / fallback rate by tenant and by route. Alert if >1% for production tenants during simulation.
- Latency delta introduced by routing change (p50/p95). Rollback if p95 increases > 200ms for high-throughput routes.
- False-positive rate (requests blocked while legal allowed) measured during simulation by comparing to reference logs.

Migration plan (phased):
1) Implement controls in simulate mode (2 weeks internal): enable for 10 pilot tenants (non-critical). Collect telemetry and run policy simulator against 14 days of historic traffic.
2) Canary (region-level, 2–3 clusters): enforce for new tenants only. Confirm block/fallback behavior and alerting.
3) Bulk opt-in (customers with opt-in flag): offer a migration window with support. Use data-migration scripts to relocate persisted objects.
4) Full enforcement: enforce for all pinned tenants; open enforcement flag for per-route overrides removed after 4 weeks.

Migration tasks (examples):
- Data export/import: tools to copy S3 objects between buckets with new residency tag and re-encrypt with regional KMS. Include integrity checks (SHA256).
- KV backfill: re-hash keys with residency and replay or invalidate old keys.
- Cached model weights: ensure model cache manager prefers local copies; purge remote caches on cutover.

Rollback and recovery:
- Quick rollback: flip enforcement_mode to simulate or off at global feature-flag level.
- Selective rollback: disable routing change in specific gateways via per-cluster flag.
- Reconciliation script: reconcile last 24 hours of blocked requests, queue them for replay once issue resolved.

Acceptance criteria for GA enforcement:
- All pilot tenants report <0.5% unexpected denials during 2-week enforce canary.
- Telemetry shows stable latency (p95 within threshold) and enforcement telemetry is complete for 100% requests.
- Legal signoff obtained for each jurisdiction (UK, EU, CA, AU).

Operational playbook (run-time):
- On receiving an enforcement alert: check enforcement telemetry dashboard -> identify tenant -> check policy_simulator output -> determine if rollback or patch.
- For customer escalations: run customer-specific replay (idempotent, bounded) and provide audit logs for requests affected.
- For capacity-driven fallbacks: verify that fallback used compatible-model-in-region first; if not, check model registry metadata.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we represent composite residency (e.g., control plane in US, data in EU) — need policy schema update.
- Edge-case: third-party plugin that stores files in central S3 (e.g., integrations) — add integration whitelist/deny list.
- Determine retention period for residency audit logs (ops vs. legal requirements).

Next steps / owners (short):
- Avery Chen: own routing proxy changes and telemetry schema.
- Priya Shah: control-plane tenant metadata + admin API changes.
- Diego Martinez: storage gateway and S3/KMS migration tooling.
- Samira Bhandari: QA plan, simulator runs, legal signoff coordinator.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- Expect additional small perf overhead on startup while region metadata populates; this is mitigated by caching policy decisions per-tenant.
- Keep enforcement_mode in simulate for at least 2 full customer billing cycles where possible.

Appendix: quick config examples (pseudo-yaml)
- tenant profile: { "tenant_id": "T-1234", "residency": "eu-west-1", "residency_policy": "strict" }
- routing header: X-Residency: eu-west-1
- audit event fields: [timestamp, tenant_id, routed_region, model_variant, enforcement_action, reason, request_id]

References and links:
- Regional Residency Spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Regional+Residency+Spec
- Jira epic: INF-822
- Migration PR (infra): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/414

End of runbook.
